title: Starter SDK hypothesis validation notebook
body:
Purpose:
This notebook collects lightweight experiments and acceptance criteria we will run during the first two sprint cycles to validate hypotheses about the Starter SDK onboarding experience. Treat as a lab log (notes-to-self + reproducible steps). Not a polished playbook — aim is fast iteration and clear pass/fail signals.

Context / motivation:
- We keep hearing that new devs stall at: auth, env setup, first request latency, and understanding cost.
- Hypothesis-driven approach lets us ship small changes (docs, telemetry, CLI) and measure impact quickly.
- Goal: reduce "time-to-first-successful-invocation" and increase retention (first-day active integration) for trial users.

Primary hypotheses (ranked):
1) Reducing setup friction by providing a single-file environment starter (one script + env var) will reduce median time-to-first-success by >= 30%.
2) Adding an explicit in-doc telemetry check and smoke-test will catch 75% of common integration failures before a support ticket is opened.
3) A 5-minute micro-syllabus (moduleized quickstart) improves conversion to second-day usage by 20% vs current free-form doc.

Success metrics (measurable signals):
- Median time-to-first-successful-invocation (TFSI) in minutes from signup -> SDK request success.
- % of new users who make >= 3 API calls within 24 hours.
- Support ticket rate for "SDK setup" category per 100 new users.
- Failure surface: % of quickstart runs that fail due to credentials vs network vs dependency mismatch.
- Telemetry coverage: % of quickstart runs that emit smoke-test event.

Experiment matrix (short experiments we can run in parallel):
A. One-step env script (env-starter.sh) vs curated multi-step doc (control)
- Sample size: 150 new signups each arm
- Instrumentation: TFSI, errors, reorder time

B. Inline smoke-test in README (curl + SDK snippet) vs separate smoke-test file (smoke_test.py)
- measure percent of users that run smoke-test within 1st hour

C. Micro-syllabus (5 modules, 5–10 minute each) delivered as a collapsible sidebar in docs vs single page
- measure second-day retention and completion rate

Lab setup (minimal reproducible environment)
- local: python3.11, virtualenv
- node: 18.x for JS snippets
- SDK branch: feature/hypothesis-starter (see linked PR)
- test account: sandbox-starter@redwood.test (use sample creds in test vault)

Quickstart smoke commands (examples to embed in doc):
- curl (env-based):
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer "$REDWOOD_API_KEY"' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Hello"}'

- Python SDK snippet (inline):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = client.generate('redwood-1-small', 'Hello')
  print(resp.text)

What to instrument (telemetry + logs):
- Hook events into quickstart runner: quickstart.started, quickstart.env-check, quickstart.smoke_success, quickstart.smoke_fail, quickstart.first_request_latency_ms
- Tag events with cohort: trial_source, doc_variant, sdk_version, region
- Capture stacktrace + OS + dependency versions on failure

Acceptance criteria for a change to be considered effective:
- Decrease median TFSI by >= 30% in experiment arm over control with p < 0.05 (bootstrap).
- Support-ticket rate for SDK-setup down by 25% in the cohort.
- Smoke-test pass rate >= 80% for new installs (target).

Mini-syllabus (5 micro-modules) — each module includes 3 quick checks:
1) Get credentials & run first curl (1–3 min) -> check quickstart.smoke_success
2) Bind SDK & run local sample app (5–7 min) -> check first_request_latency_ms
3) Understanding costs: token counting & request profiling (5 min) -> include sample billing snippet
4) Safety & limits: rate limits, retries, error codes (5 min) -> show deterministic retry pseudocode
5) Promote to staging: wiring env + CI smoke test + telemetry (10 min)

Rollout & gating plan:
- Internal beta (eng + docs): 1 week to gather initial signals.
- Canary to 5% of new signups for 2 weeks.
- If acceptance criteria pass, 100% roll for new documentation; backfill a "migration note" for existing docs.

Failure modes & fallback strategies:
- If one-step env script causes confusion (overwrites existing env) -> switch to prompt that creates "redwood.env.sample" and requires copy command.
- If smoke-test increases support noise (users copy sample API key) -> make sample keys inert and show clear warning copy.

Unresolved questions (to research quickly):
- Which OS/package manager mismatch is the most common (pip vs pipx vs brew)? We need real data from onboarding logs.
- Should the CLI create a minimal project scaffold or leave that to templates? (pro/con in notes)

Quick TODOs (owner tags):
- [Aisha] Draft env-starter.sh and sample README snippets (DUE: 2025-03-28)
- [Jinsoo] Add telemetry events to SDK smoke harness (DUE: 2025-03-24)
- [Maria] Run initial 30-person internal beta and synthesize notes (DUE: 2025-03-21)
- [PM] Align with Growth on cohort selection and success KPI mapping (JIRA: JIRA-PI-789)

Notes-to-self and heuristics (informal):
- Keep friction small: a single clearly highlighted code block at the top of doc works better than nested steps.
- Error copy must be actionable (tell the dev what to check first).
- Add a "How to debug" inline checklist (network, env var, key scopes).

Meeting snapshot (2025-03-18):
- Quick consensus: start with env script + README inline smoke-test.
- Action: instrument telemetry before external canary.

Appendix: reproducible smoke-test runner (local)
- python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
- pip install -e ./sdk[dev]
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
- python examples/smoke_test.py

End / next steps:
- Merge small docs + telemetry changes behind feature flag.
- Build dashboard (quickstart funnel) in Console: steps completed per new user.
- Re-evaluate after 2 full weeks of canary traffic.

-- Aisha (notes, iterating)
